newsitem.title: UK: London & Overseas Freighters delays AGM.
newsitem.headline: London & Overseas Freighters delays AGM.

text.p: London & Overseas Freighters Plc said Monday it has not set a date for its annual general meeting due to its ongoing process to explore long term strategic options open to the company.

London & Overseas made the statement as it reported net income of $824,000 for the fourth quarter ended March 31, 1997, compared with a net loss of $435,000 for the equivalent year-ago period. Net operating income rose to $2.575 million from $1.712 million, it added.

Referring to its move announced on February 27 to explore a range of strategic alternatives aimed at positioning itself to compete more effectively and enhance shareholder value, the Bermuda-based shipping company said: "No further comment is appropriate at this time."
It said that due to the timing of this process it had decided not to publish an annual report at this stage or set a date for an AGM.
"A full statement will be made and meeting dates set in due course," it added.
A number of companies have expressed an initial interest in London & Overseas, according to industry sources, but a decision is not expected for about six weeks.
London & Overseas also said on Monday that short term prospects were benefiting its trading.
"Voyage earnings on both our Panamax and Suezmax fleets, for the quarter to date are running significantly ahead of the levels reported," it said.

The company said its fourth quarter results had benefited from a 20 percent improvement in time charter equivalent earnings for its three Panamax vessels "as a result of particular strength in the Caribbean market".

"Our Suezmax fleet continued to produce a strong and stable result, averaging $25,500 for the quarter," London & Overseas added. It operates three Suezmax ships. --Paul Berrill Reuters Shipping News + 44 171 542 4087
